svg.title: From nothing to a working kubeconfig — every command, in order

g.text: From nothing to a working kubeconfig — every command, in order
STAGE A · on YOUR machine — Kubernetes is not involved yet
STAGE B · hand it to Kubernetes
STAGE C · an ADMIN approves — the CA signs
STAGE D · collect the signed certificate
STAGE E · assemble the kubeconfig
1 · a private key
openssl genrsa -out batman.key 4096
NEVER leaves your machine and is never sent anywhere
2 · a Certificate Signing Request, signed by that key
openssl req -new -key batman.key -out batman.csr \
-subj “/CN=batman/O=cluster-superheroes” -sha256
CN = the USERNAME you are asking for · O = the GROUP you are asking for
A request, not a grant. Anyone can ask for anything.
3 · base64 the CSR and build the API object
CSR_DATA=$(base64 batman.csr | tr -d '\n') ← tr strips the line wraps
CSR_USER=batman
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1 · kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata.name: ${CSR_USER} ← the OBJECT name, NOT the username
spec.request: ${CSR_DATA}
spec.signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
spec.usages: [client auth] ← required by that signer
4 · submit it
kubectl apply -f batman-csr-request.yaml
kubectl get csr → CONDITION: Pending · REQUESTOR: system:admin
5 · approval
kubectl certificate approve batman
kubectl get csr batman → CONDITION: Approved,Issued
kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client is NEVER auto-approved — a human with RBAC
permission on certificatesigningrequests/approval must act. THIS is the control.
And the CertificateSubjectRestriction admission plugin blocks O=system:masters outright.
6 · extract it
kubectl get csr batman -o jsonpath='{.status.certificate}' | base64 -d > batman.crt
openssl x509 -in batman.crt -noout -subject -issuer -dates ← check what you actually got
7 · start from a copy and strip the old identity — KEEP the cluster block
cp /.kube/config batman.config
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl config unset users.default
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl config delete-context default
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl config unset current-context
→ users: null · contexts: null · clusters: KEPT (the server URL and the CA public cert)
The cluster block is the half of chapter 05-02 that is not a secret — reuse it.
8 · add the new credentials and a context
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl config set-credentials batman \
--client-certificate=batman.crt --client-key=batman.key --embed-certs=true
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl config set-context batman --cluster=default --user=batman
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl config use-context batman
9 · use it
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl get nodes → works
KUBECONFIG=batman.config kubectl run nginx --image=nginx → pod/nginx created
...because O=cluster-superheroes matches the ClusterRoleBinding from chapter 05-03.
Change the O and the same pipeline produces an identity that can do nothing.
Nine commands, and not one of them created a user object — because none exists to create. The only thing Kubernetes stored was a CertificateSigningRequest, and even that is deleted afterwards.
What persists is a signed certificate on a laptop whose Subject the cluster will believe. spurin/kubeconfig-creator wraps exactly these steps into one script with five stages.
